report.root_cause: The 08:03 deploy for ticket OPS-250 (raise max-players 20->40) overwrote server.properties and also set white-list=true and enforce-whitelist=true (both were false in deploy/previous/server.properties). whitelist.json was empty ([]), so every connection was rejected with "You are not whitelisted on this server!", including the regular players Alex_Builds and Steve_Mines.
report.actions: Checked status and logs; saw every join rejected by the whitelist from about 08:03:45. Declared the incident. Compared server.properties with deploy/previous/server.properties and deploy/2026-11-01-server-properties.md, which showed the unintended whitelist change. Rewrote server.properties keeping max-players=40 and setting white-list=false and enforce-whitelist=false, matching the previous values. Restarted the server (no players were online at that point) so the properties took effect. Verified after restart: Alex_Builds and Steve_Mines joined and stayed connected; TPS 20, MSPT under 1, heap about 411 MB of 768 MB. Did not modify whitelist.json, the world, or any player data, and did not ban anyone.
report.residual_risk: Whitelist is now off, as it was before the deploy. A recurring pattern of unknown accounts (newplayer01 through newplayer60, all connecting from 127.0.0.1) joined and left repeatedly; newplayer60 was still online at last check. online-mode is false, so usernames are not authenticated. I did not ban them because there was no evidence they were malicious. Ops should decide whether to re-enable the whitelist properly (populate whitelist.json first), investigate the connection churn, and review the OPS-250 deploy so unrelated whitelist settings are not changed again.
